title: Balancing exploration vs hand-holding in game design
author: schmighaar
selftext:
Hey, 40 something graphic designer here who jumped on the vibe coding games bandwaggon. I have a question that is more about game design than tools or AI, Hope someone can help. 

I grew up on the snes. I remember games that were hard, sometimes cryptic, and didn't explain everything. You just had to explore and figure out everthing as you went along. I remember struggling a bit on rpgs as a kid, english wasnt my first language, but figuring things out was part of the fun. 

I’m older, and I prefer old 2d games. I like puzzles, strategy, rpgs and word games like wordle or scrabble. For the past month, I’ve been vibe coding 2d cyberpunk tactics mobile game that combines all those elements.

I didn’t try to clone an existing game but reallly went in with my own ideas and concepts, although I was liberal with my inspirations. Im designing the assets in figma, drawing some art on procreate and writing the story, designing the mechanics and getting a friend to work on the soundtrack. I’m working really hard each pass and revisions to go over what claude spits out and edit and change and try to desloppify it and making it my own. 

The game is presented through a fictional cyberdeck OS in a cyberpunk world. You're roleplaying as the person using the cyberdeck to control a rebel group, through the interface.  You’re never in the battlefield, you’re the tacticien, working remotely. The story unfolds gradually, and new mechanics unlock as you progress, as apps on the cyberdeck. 

The problem is that when I showed it to friends, nobody really got it. Same thing with a few people here on Reddit who tried it. I've since improved the UI/UX and added a tutorial with small micro missions that teach you through gameplay, added some tutorial hints in popups and through character conversations. It's better, but people still seem confused not knowing what to do where to click or which character they are…

I'm wondering if I'm trying too hard to let players discover things on their own, or if people just expect more guidance nowadays. Or maybe my instructions arent clear enough, or the ux still need work. 

How do you decide what needs to be explained versus what players should figure out for themselves? How do you make a game challenging and mysterious without making it confusing?

Curious to hear how other devs approach this, especially with unconventional mechanics or interfaces.

comments.author: No-Revenue-7707
comments.body:
首先向您问好。

现在的游戏在逐渐简单化，像是自动化寻路，地图一键传送等功能越来越多。

我26岁，大约从我八岁开始就接触不同的游戏。我能和您分享的是，我对于复杂缺乏引导的游戏越来越缺乏耐心。

我时常会给自己这个心态找理由：工作已经够麻烦了，我为什么还要在游戏里被上课去学习游戏里的知识。

能给您的建议是：希望您整合一下游戏的系统，然后为每个系统制作傻瓜式新手引导，然后将它们安插在这个系统开放的那一关或者那一等级阶段。

如果系统全部在开局开放，那您不得不考虑只保留一到两个系统去作为开局，然后其他系统逐步开放给玩家。

replies.author: No-Revenue-7707
replies.body:
顺便一提，按照您的描述我非常感兴趣您的游戏。

不知道哪里可以找到您开发的游戏？

replies.author: schmighaar
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback. I did try to introduce the different mechanics slowly but it still not enough. I might add more micro missions at the beginning and work on the ux ui some more. You can try the game [here](http://grimpixels.com/trace), let me know your thoughts!
